messages:
Mike: Heads up — after yesterday's pool-change PR we started seeing sporadic OOMs on canary and p99 token latency up ~40% for chat workloads. Repro: canary region, 2x concurrent short-chat streams. Logs show 'cuda out of memory: tried to allocate 22.0MB'.

Anna: Is this the PR that switched to single-scratchpad-per-device reuse? (PR #4021)

Mike: Yes — changed scratchpad lifetime to cross-request reuse and removed eager_free in a few hot paths.

Sara: Seen similar on nightly. perf-bot shows GC events increased and KV cache thrash: eviction rate jumped from 0.6% -> 4.2%.

perf-bot: Canary stats: p50=18ms p95=84ms p99=220ms (baseline p99=160ms). KV_eviction_rate=4.2%.

Dave: Can you paste the alloc logs? Also which kernel selection path hit? I suspect large-batch matmul kernel was chosen incorrectly due to sequence-length distribution shift.

Mike: Quick alloc logs excerpt + grep:
```
[2026-03-17T11:02:13Z] alloc slab_id=3 sz=12.8MB reuse=true
[2026-03-17T11:02:13Z] kv_cache_hit=false eviction=LRU slab_fragment=42%
[2026-03-17T11:02:13Z] cuda out of memory: tried to allocate 22.0MB
```

Anna: slab_fragmentation=42% is pretty high. I remember the PR lowered min_slab_size from 8MB -> 4MB which can increase fragmentation for lots of small activations.

Sara: Quick mitigations to try: 1) re-enable eager_free for logits/scratchpad buffers, 2) add per-request workspace cap (e.g., 64MB) to bound peaks, 3) tweak batching heuristic to avoid mixing very different seq_len buckets.

Dave: Also add a defensive check in kernel selection: if estimated kv_cache_pressure > threshold, prefer a kernel that requires less working memory even if slightly slower. That will reduce eviction churn.

Mike: Ran a 2h canary with eager_free=true and workspace_cap=64MB. No OOMs and p99 moved back to ~170ms.

perf-bot: Canary (mitigations) stats: p50=19ms p95=78ms p99=172ms KV_eviction=0.9%.

Anna: Good. Next steps: rollout mitigations to all canaries, then implement slab compaction (coalesce free segments) and a reuse-watermark that disables cross-request reuse when fragmentation >30%.

Sara: I'll open a follow-up issue listing: 1) slab compaction background pass, 2) reuse watermark + telemetry, 3) per-model max_scratchpad config, 4) A/B for eager_free perf memory tradeoffs.

Mike: Thx — I put up PR #4030 to partially revert the cross-request reuse change so we can buy time while we implement compaction.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy for rev-4030 started at 2026-03-17T13:10:02Z :rocket:

Anna: If regressions persist after the revert, consider per-tenant scratchpad pools (more conservative isolation) as a temporary fallback.

Mike: Agreed. Will post updated metrics tomorrow AM and keep the canary pinned for 24h.

Sara: TL;DR: reuse optimization improved steady-state throughput in ideal cases but increased fragmentation and KV churn under mixed short/long traffic -> caused latency regression + OOMs. Short-term fix = eager_free + workspace cap; long-term = compaction, reuse watermark, smarter kernel selection.

Dave: Also add a perf-test that simulates mixed seq_len bursts to catch this during CI (synthetic KV churn).

Mike: Noted. I'll prototype the CI workload and share the harness.

Anna: Thanks everyone — good catch and quick rollback path.
